question: The Commission recently announced its presence on W Social shortly after publishing its strategy on the future of virtual worlds and web technologies, while maintaining accounts on ActivityPub-based services. At the same time, concerns have been raised regarding the Commission’s promotion of specific commercial social media platforms and the absence of a coherent approach to digital public infrastructure. In this context: 1.

Why did the Commission choose to establish a presence on the closed-source platform W Social immediately after publishing a strategy that emphasises openness, rather than operating its own Atmosphere servers as it does for its ActivityPub presence?

Does the Commission intend to publish a comprehensive social media strategy addressing both its communications objectives and its approach to European technological sovereignty, including whether it will prioritise open digital infrastructure and interoperable ecosystems over dependence on proprietary platforms?

Does the Commission consider it appropriate, in the light of the applicable ethics rules in the Code of Conduct, for the Commission President to publish content on her Instagram account that could reasonably be perceived as promoting specific commercial social media companies?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.9.2026) Establishing presence on the European social media platform W is part of the Commission’s continued approach to diversify its presence on social media and to reach out to as many Europeans as possible.

The content posted on the Commission’s account on W is fully accessible to the public through the interoperable Authenticated Transfer Protocol as well as through the web. The Commission continues to provide strong policy and implementation support for interoperability and open digital ecosystems, including open standards, open source solutions and European digital public infrastructures.

This commitment is reflected in a range of concrete initiatives, such as sovereign cloud procurement1, code.europa.eu, and the EU Open Source Solutions Catalogue2, which facilitates the publication, discovery and reuse of open source solutions across the EU public sector.

The recently adopted Open Source Strategy3 provides that the Commission will seek to strengthen the open source media space by supporting open and decentralised social media solutions and platforms. Posts on corporate accounts aim to promote the presence and activities on social media and do not imply endorsement of any commercial service or business model.
